stimulus.text:
“Among the numerous advantages promised by a well constructed Union, none deserves to be more accurately developed than its tendency to break and control the violence of faction. . . . By a faction, I understand a number of citizens, whether amounting to a majority or a minority of the whole, who are united and actuated by some common impulse of passion, or of interest, adversed to the rights of other citizens, or to the permanent and aggregate interests of the community. . . . Extend the sphere, and you take in a greater variety of parties and interests; you make it less probable that a majority of the whole will have a common motive to invade the rights of other citizens.”

—Publius (James Madison), Federalist No. 10, New York Daily Advertiser, November 22, 1787

books.section: Topic 3.8 The Constitutional Convention and Debates over Ratification, C. Federalists, Anti-Federalists, and the Adoption of the Bill of Rights

stem: According to Madison, what is a faction?

options.text: A political party that wins an election fairly
options.misconception: Winning an election fairly does not make a group a faction; Madison defines faction by its motive, not its victory.

options.text: A foreign government that interferes in American affairs
options.misconception: Madison's faction is a group of citizens inside the republic, not a foreign government.

options.text: Citizens united by a passion or interest against the rights of others
A small state that refuses to follow the laws of Congress
options.misconception: A state refusing laws is not Madison's definition; a faction is a group of citizens, large or small.

rationales.C: Madison defines a faction in the passage itself: citizens, majority or minority, united by a common impulse of passion or interest, opposed to the rights of others or to the permanent interests of the community.
rationales.A: Fair electoral victory is not the test; Madison's test is a motive opposed to others' rights or the common good.
rationales.B: A faction is made of citizens inside the republic, not a foreign government.
rationales.D: A faction is a group of citizens, not a state refusing a law.
rationales.general:
1. Find Madison's definition: By a faction, I understand a number of citizens.
2. The group may be a majority or a minority of the whole.
3. What makes it a faction is a common impulse of passion or interest, opposed to the rights of others or the good of the whole.
4. The definition turns on motive, not on size or on winning.
Remember: a definition answers what a thing is, so use the writer's own words.
